title: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic: Adaptive Switching Costs for Robust Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.14099v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deliberation costs are commonly used in hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to prevent options from collapsing to primitive actions. Existing approaches rely on fixed penalties or duration-based adaptations, both of which are indirect proxies for an option's utility. This paper argues that option persistence should instead depend on the opportunity cost of abandoning the current behavior. We propose the Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic ($OC^2$) framework, which defines a state-dependent deliberation cost using the positive value gap between the active option and its best alternative. This encourages persistence when the current option is clearly preferable and allows rapid switching when a better option emerges. We show that directly learning such costs leads to a degenerate zero-cost solution and introduces an auxiliary objective that aligns the learned cost with the value-gap target. The approach is evaluated in Four Rooms and Pinb

translated_title: 机会成本Option-Critic：面向鲁棒分层强化学习的自适应切换成本
translated_abstract: 深思成本在分层强化学习（HRL）中通常被用于防止选项退化为原始动作。现有方法依赖于固定惩罚或基于持续时间的自适应调整，但这两者都是选项效用的间接代理指标。本文认为，选项的持续性应当取决于放弃当前行为的机会成本。我们提出了机会成本Option-Critic（OC²）框架，该框架利用当前活跃选项与其最佳备选选项之间的正向价值差距来定义一个依赖于状态的深思成本。这使得当当前选项明显更优时鼓励其持续执行，而当出现更优选项时则允许快速切换。我们证明了直接学习此类成本会导致退化的零成本解，因此引入了一个辅助目标，使学习到的成本与价值差距目标对齐。该方法在Four Rooms和Pinball环境中进行了评估。
tldr: 该论文提出机会成本Option-Critic（OC²）框架，利用当前选项与最佳备选选项之间的价值差距来定义自适应的状态依赖切换成本，从而实现更鲁棒的分层强化学习。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic (OC²) framework, which defines adaptive state-dependent deliberation costs based on the value gap between the active option and its best alternative, enabling robust hierarchical reinforcement learning.
